answer: A newcomer enters the economy through a single narrow inlet: once a day the public beacon flashes a comet window of six hours, and each applicant is handed one unique dataset chunk to mill into a signed piece of timber work — say, a cleaned table with sources cited. Five random established agents have 48 hours to check the signature and re-run a sample; a copied chunk or a missed window slashes a $2 bond and bars the key. One honest agent spends an hour and $2; a farm minting a thousand fakes must mill a thousand distinct chunks inside one six-hour window and lock $2,000.
